summary.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Its familiar sun-and-moon shape gives an immediate association with light, but the sources also describe an early form combining the moon with a window. The historical question is how those forms relate: the supplied accounts disagree about whether sun and moon were already an ancient construction.

history.text: Dong Chinese presents moonlight through a window as the original image and rejects the sun-and-moon explanation. Wiktionary instead reports both constructions in oracle-bone writing, identifying the window form as 朙 and saying that the Shuowen treated it as standard.

uncertainties.text: These excerpts cannot establish which construction came first or whether one arose from the other. The sun-and-moon reading is a useful explanation of the familiar shape, while a claim about its historical priority would require closer examination of the early forms.
